subject: Planned graceful IO evacuation for eastus3 - maintenance window Jun 1, 2026
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: ops@starlight.ai, engleads@acme.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planned graceful IO evacuation for eastus3 - maintenance window Jun 1, 2026

Hello —

We are writing to share a scheduled maintenance window for eastus3 that will involve a staged IO driver refresh and graceful node evacuation. This work is preventive and intended to improve long-term stability for inference workloads that are sensitive to transient IO regressions.

Summary
- Window: Jun 1, 2026 00:30–04:30 UTC (May 31 17:30–21:30 PDT)
- Scope: eastus3 host IO driver update + rolling graceful evacuation of serving nodes (no full-region-wide outage expected)
- Impact: brief connection failovers (few seconds–1 minute) for individual requests during node reattach; overall capacity preserved via staggered drains
- Customer-facing mitigation: we will maintain a canary group and reduce drain concurrency for accounts with strict latency SLAs if requested

What we ask from you
- No action required for most customers. If you have pinned instances in eastus3 or specific affinity rules, reply to this thread and we will coordinate a reduced-concurrency path for your traffic.
- If you operate time-sensitive jobs, flag them and we will whitelist or shift maintenance timing.

Attachments
- eastus3-io-evac-runbook.pdf (runbook)
- io-driver-change-log.txt (driver notes)

We will post live updates to the status page and the runbook link above. If you'd like a pre-window call, nominate a time and we’ll set it up. Thanks for your patience — the update reduces observed IO latency variance on several hot paths.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Production Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: ops@starlight.ai
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned graceful IO evacuation for eastus3 - maintenance window Jun 1, 2026

Thanks for the heads up. Starlight AI runs nightly batch scoring at 02:00 UTC which overlaps the window. Can you confirm whether those longer-running jobs may be interrupted or retried? If so wed like to opt-in to reduced concurrency for our tenant.

— Jess (ops@starlight.ai)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: ops@starlight.ai, engleads@acme.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned graceful IO evacuation for eastus3 - maintenance window Jun 1, 2026

Hi Jess —
Thanks, good question. The maintenance is designed so long-running batch jobs are unlikely to be killed; we will perform graceful drain and allow in-flight requests to finish where possible. However, depending on queueing and host-level timeouts, retries can happen.

Options we can offer for Starlight AI:
- Reduced drain concurrency: we limit the number of nodes drained at once for your tenant to minimize parallel interruptions (this is our default offer for customers with critical batch jobs).
- Window shift: we can move maintenance for hosts serving only your tenancy to a later slot, if the bulk of your work is outside the proposed window.

Please confirm youd like reduced drain concurrency and well apply the policy and send an updated runbook with the opt-in reflected.

Ive attached the runbook and change log; internal run timeline is in the linked Jira (OPS-4321).

— Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: post-maintenance follow-up plan for eastus3 (prep notes)

Laura / Grace —

Following the customer confirmations we received (Starlight opted into reduced concurrency), please track the following as part of our post-maintenance follow-up:

Action items (post-run)
- Ops: collect node-level IO latency histograms and KV cache hit-rates for the 12 hours pre/post window (owner: Laura)
- SE: verify Starlight AI tenant did not observe >1% failed request spike and log any customer-side retries for correlation (owner: Grace)
- Product: prepare a short postmortem note for customers summarizing observed impact and any driver rollbacks (owner: Markus)
- Compliance: save runbook and signed run approvals to the SOC2 evidence bucket (link in runbook)

Ill draft the customer-facing postmortem and circulate. Also create OPS-4321-POST as the follow-up ticket and link the metrics.

— Markus
